definitions.explanation: The sour taste quality, one of the five basic tastes. Found in citrus fruits, vinegar, and fermented foods.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{酸味|さんみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧。
examples.english: This apple has a strong sourness.

examples.japanese: ⟦レモン→レモン：10456_remon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{酸味|さんみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる→引き立てる：12585_hikitateru⟧。
examples.english: The acidity of lemon enhances the dish.

examples.japanese: {酸味|さんみ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{甘味|あまみ}→甘味：07017_amami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦バランス→バランス：03870_baransu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: The balance between sourness and sweetness is good.

notes:
{酸味|さんみ} is sourness or acidity considered as a quality of a food or drink — one of the five basic tastes. It is the standard word in cooking, and in describing coffee, wine, and fruit.

Formation: ⟦{酸|さん}→酸：28620_san⟧ 'acid' + {味|み} 'taste.' The same 〜{味|み} suffix names the other tastes below.

Note the part of speech: {酸味|さんみ} is a noun naming the quality, so it is something a food ⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧ or weak in. To call something sour directly, use the i-adjective ⟦{酸|す}っぱい→酸っぱい：02346_suppai⟧. {酸味|さんみ} is also the more appreciative of the two: ⟦{酸|す}っぱい→酸っぱい：02346_suppai⟧ often suggests something has gone off, while {酸味|さんみ} usually describes a flavour worth having.

Collocations:
- {酸味|さんみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧: strongly sour
- {酸味|さんみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧: to add acidity
- {酸味|さんみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{利|き}いている→利く：11845_kiku⟧: has a pleasant tang

The five basic tastes:
- ⟦{甘味|あまみ}→甘味：07017_amami⟧: sweetness
- {酸味|さんみ}: sourness
- ⟦{塩味|しおあじ}→塩味：12106_shioaji⟧ / ⟦{塩気|しおけ}→塩気：07018_shioke⟧: saltiness
- ⟦{苦味|にがみ}→苦味：14101_nigami⟧: bitterness
- ⟦{旨味|うまみ}→旨味：06998_umami⟧: umami, savouriness
